tools.name: publish_sparkplug
tools.description:
WRITE: publish a Sparkplug B message. Set message_type and give only the arguments of that mode.

Requires MQTT_WRITES_ENABLED=true; otherwise returns success:false (meta.code 'writes_disabled') and publishes nothing.

As this server's own edge node (SPARKPLUG_GROUP_ID/SPARKPLUG_EDGE_NODE_ID, see get_broker_info; never the ID of a real edge node):
- NBIRTH (metrics?): make this server an edge node and publish its birth. The first NBIRTH reconnects with an NDEATH Last Will carrying a new bdSeq, so the broker announces the node's death if the server disappears. bdSeq and 'Node Control/Rebirth' are added for you; seq is 0. Publishing NBIRTH again is a rebirth: devices must then be born again. After an unexpected disconnect the node is dead and needs a new NBIRTH.
- NDEATH: take the node offline (QoS 1, confirmed by the broker). Its devices count as dead; the next NBIRTH uses a new bdSeq.
- DBIRTH (device_id, metrics): birth of a device of this node. Needs a born node.
- DDEATH (device_id): death of a device born with DBIRTH.
- NDATA (metrics): new values of the node's metrics. Needs a born node.
- DDATA (device_id, metrics): new values of a device born with DBIRTH.
These use the node's next seq. The server does not act on commands sent to its own node.

Commands to other edge nodes, which can change real equipment:
- NCMD (edge_node_id, metrics, group_id?): e.g. {"name": "Node Control/Rebirth", "value": true, "type": "boolean"} asks a node to republish its births.
- DCMD (edge_node_id, device_id, metrics, group_id?): the edge node applies the metrics to the device.

Sent at most once. success:true (meta.outcome 'written') means the message was written to the network (QoS 0, as the specification requires; NDEATH: acknowledged by the broker). For a command that does not mean the node applied it: read its next NDATA or DDATA with read_messages to confirm. meta.outcome 'not_sent' means nothing left the server. 'unknown' (meta.code 'outcome_unknown') means it may have gone out: the server never sends it again, so check before retrying.

Metrics are a list of {"name": str, "value": ..., "type": str} objects. type is one of int8, int16, int32 (or int), int64 (or long), uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64, float, double, boolean (or bool), string, text, uuid, datetime (milliseconds since the Unix epoch) or bytes (value as a hex string), case-insensitive, so the datatype names list_sparkplug_nodes shows (Int32, Double, ...) work too. The value must match the type and fit its range; null sends a null metric. An invalid metric is refused before anything is sent. For int64, uint64 and datetime values, plain decimal strings are accepted to preserve precision through JSON clients.

message_type.description: The Sparkplug B message to publish; it decides which other arguments apply (see the tool description). NBIRTH, NDEATH, DBIRTH, DDEATH, NDATA and DDATA are published by this server's own edge node; NCMD and DCMD are commands to other edge nodes and devices.

name.description: Metric name, e.g. 'temperature' or 'Node Control/Rebirth'. Unique within a birth.

value.description: The value. It must match type and fit its range: an integer for the int types, a number for float/double, true/false for boolean, a string for string/text/uuid, milliseconds since the Unix epoch for datetime, a hex string for bytes. null sends a null metric.

type.description: Sparkplug B datatype, case-insensitive: int8, int16, int32 (or int), int64 (or long), uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64, float, double, boolean (or bool), string, text, uuid, datetime (milliseconds since the Unix epoch) or bytes (value as a hex string). The datatype names list_sparkplug_nodes and read_messages show (Int32, Double, Boolean, ...) are accepted as they are.

metrics.description: The metrics to publish. NBIRTH: the node's metrics (optional; bdSeq and 'Node Control/Rebirth' are added by the server). DBIRTH: every metric of the device (may be empty). NDATA, DDATA, NCMD, DCMD: at least one. Not used by NDEATH and DDEATH.

device_id.description: DBIRTH, DDEATH, DDATA: a device of this server's own edge node. DCMD: the target device. Any non-empty text without '+', '/' or '#'.

edge_node_id.description: NCMD, DCMD: the target edge node (required; there is no default target). Any non-empty text without '+', '/' or '#'.

group_id.description: NCMD, DCMD: the target group. Default: SPARKPLUG_GROUP_ID (see get_broker_info). Any non-empty text without '+', '/' or '#'.

delivery.description: What the success confirms about delivery.

seq.description: Sequence number (this server's own node only).

metrics.description: Number of metrics in the payload.

error.description: What went wrong, when success is false.

code.description: Why the call failed; set whenever success is false. See the contract's errors.

note.description: A hint about an empty or surprising result.

outcome.description: written: sent (QoS 1/2: acknowledged). not_sent: nothing left the server. unknown: it may have reached the broker; check before retrying. rejected: an explicit refusal that guarantees nothing was applied (never reported over MQTT 3.1.1).

request_sent.description: Whether the request may have left the server; null means an unexpected failure prevented dispatch tracking. Treat a null value as an unknown outcome and check before retrying.

tools.name: get_broker_info
tools.description: Report this server's connection to the MQTT broker and its configuration. Call it first: it says whether the broker is reachable (connected, last_error), whether writes are allowed (writes_enabled: while it is false every publish is refused), which subscriptions are held, how many received messages are buffered, and the state of this server's own Sparkplug B edge node. Does not contact the broker, so it answers even while the broker is down.

broker.description: Broker URL; credentials are never shown.

writes_enabled.description: Whether the publish tools may send (MQTT_WRITES_ENABLED).

items.description: A subscription this server holds, with the QoS the broker granted.

sparkplug.description: This server's own Sparkplug B edge node.

node_lost.description: Why the node died unexpectedly (its NDEATH will was published), or null.

enabled.description: Native config gate only; not policy, reachability or device permission.

registry.description: Observed Sparkplug cache and loss counters, not a complete broker inventory.

error.description: What went wrong, when success is false.

code.description: Why the call failed; set whenever success is false. See the contract's errors.

note.description: A hint about an empty or surprising result.

tools.name: subscribe_topic
tools.description: Subscribe this server to an MQTT topic filter, so that matching messages are kept for read_messages. MQTT is publish/subscribe: nothing can be read from a topic until this server is subscribed to it, and only messages that arrive afterwards are seen, plus the topic's retained message, which the broker sends at once. Subscribe to 'spBv1.0/#' to discover Sparkplug B edge nodes with list_sparkplug_nodes. Succeeds only once the broker acknowledges (SUBACK); data.granted_qos is the QoS it granted. Subscriptions are restored automatically after a reconnect. Changes broker/client subscription state; special broker filters can affect other consumers. Explicit read_only policy denies this operation.

topic.description: Topic filter. '+' matches exactly one level, '#' (only as the whole last level) matches everything below. Filters starting with '$' other than '$SYS/' are broker extensions (shared $share/ and $queue/, exclusive $exclusive/) that change what other clients receive; they are refused unless writes are enabled.

qos.description: Highest QoS the broker may use to deliver matching messages to this server: 0 (at most once), 1 (at least once) or 2 (exactly once). The broker may grant less; data.granted_qos is what it granted. Default 0.

error.description: What went wrong, when success is false.

code.description: Why the call failed; set whenever success is false. See the contract's errors.

note.description: A hint about an empty or surprising result.

tools.name: unsubscribe_topic
tools.description: Remove one of this server's subscriptions, named exactly as list_subscriptions shows it. Messages already buffered stay readable with read_messages. Fails with meta.code 'not_subscribed' if this server holds no subscription with that exact filter. Changes broker/client subscription state and is denied by explicit read_only policy.

topic.description: A filter exactly as list_subscriptions shows it, e.g. 'sensors/#'. Filters are compared as text: unsubscribing 'sensors/temp' does not end a 'sensors/#' subscription.

error.description: What went wrong, when success is false.

code.description: Why the call failed; set whenever success is false. See the contract's errors.

note.description: A hint about an empty or surprising result.

tools.name: list_subscriptions
tools.description: List the topic filters this server is subscribed to, with the QoS the broker granted for each. Only this server's own subscriptions: the broker's other clients are not visible. Does not contact the broker.

items.description: A subscription this server holds, with the QoS the broker granted.

error.description: What went wrong, when success is false.

code.description: Why the call failed; set whenever success is false. See the contract's errors.

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description:
Return messages this server received on its subscriptions, oldest first. Only messages that arrived after subscribe_topic are available, and only the newest MQTT_MESSAGE_BUFFER_SIZE (default 1000) are kept. Each message has an increasing id, topic, qos, retain flag, received_at (UTC), payload (UTF-8 text, or hex for binary and Sparkplug payloads) and, for Sparkplug B topics, the decoded payload under 'sparkplug'.

To follow a topic, pass meta.last_id of the previous call as since_id. meta.has_more is true when more messages matched than limit allowed (with since_id, call again with the new meta.last_id for the rest). meta.missed_messages is true when messages after since_id were already pushed out of the buffer, and meta.dropped_total counts every message the buffer has pushed out. Does not contact the broker. The inbox also has an 8 MiB serialized-content budget; byte-budget eviction increments dropped_total and reports missed_messages. Integer scalars outside +/-9007199254740991 are decimal strings; non-finite floating scalars are NaN/Infinity/-Infinity strings. Metrics carry value_encoding when converted.

topic_filter.description: Only messages whose topic matches this filter ('+' and '#' allowed), e.g. 'sensors/+/temperature'. It filters what is buffered; it does not subscribe. Default: every buffered message.

limit.description: At most this many messages, 1-1000. Default 50.

since_id.description: Only messages with an id greater than this, oldest first. Pass meta.last_id of the previous call to get only what arrived since. Omitted, the newest limit messages are returned (oldest first). Ids start again at 1 when the server restarts.

id.description: Increasing id; pass the last one as since_id to read only newer messages.

datatype.description: Sparkplug datatype name, e.g. 'Int32', or null if the metric carries none and none is known.

value_encoding.description: Present when a numeric scalar is encoded as a lossless JSON string.

error.description: What went wrong, when success is false.

code.description: Why the call failed; set whenever success is false. See the contract's errors.

note.description: A hint about an empty or surprising result.

has_more.description: More messages matched than limit allowed.

dropped_total.description: Messages pushed out of the full buffer since the server started.

missed_messages.description: Messages after since_id were already pushed out of the buffer.

tools.name: list_sparkplug_nodes
tools.description: List the Sparkplug B edge nodes and devices seen in messages this server received, with their online state, bdSeq and latest metric values. Each metric shows its Sparkplug datatype, which publish_sparkplug accepts as the metric type of a command. Discovery is passive: a node appears only after one of its NBIRTH, NDATA, NDEATH, DBIRTH, DDATA or DDEATH messages arrives on a subscription this server holds, so subscribe to 'spBv1.0/#' (or 'spBv1.0/<group>/#') first. Births are not retained, so a node born before the subscription shows up with its next data message; metrics that its data messages send without a datatype then show their raw stored value until the node is reborn. online is null when unknown, for example after this server reconnected. data.this_server is the edge node this server itself publishes as (publish_sparkplug). Does not contact the broker. The observed registry is bounded to 256 nodes and 4 MiB serialized state including alias tables. meta.registry reports eviction, decode rejection and connection gaps; it is not proof of a complete broker inventory. Integer scalars outside +/-9007199254740991 are decimal strings; non-finite floating scalars are NaN/Infinity/-Infinity strings. Metrics carry value_encoding when converted.

online.description: true/false from its births, data and deaths; null when unknown.

last_seen.description: UTC time of its last message, ISO 8601.

tools.name: decode_sparkplug_payload
tools.description: Decode a hex-encoded Sparkplug B protobuf payload into its timestamp, seq and metrics (name, alias, timestamp, datatype, value). read_messages already decodes Sparkplug topics under 'sparkplug'; use this for a payload from elsewhere. Signed integers are shown as signed numbers when the metric carries its datatype; a metric without one (allowed in DATA and CMD messages) shows its raw stored value. Protobuf cannot tell every other byte string apart, so success does not prove the bytes came from a Sparkplug node. Decoded input is limited to 65536 bytes. Integer scalars outside +/-9007199254740991 are decimal strings; non-finite floating scalars are NaN/Infinity/-Infinity strings. Metrics carry value_encoding when converted.

payload_hex.description: The payload bytes as hex, as read_messages shows a Sparkplug payload (payload_encoding 'hex'). Spaces and a 0x prefix are ignored.

tools.name: publish_message
tools.description:
WRITE: publish a UTF-8 text message to an MQTT topic.

Requires MQTT_WRITES_ENABLED=true; otherwise returns success:false (meta.code 'writes_disabled') and publishes nothing.

Any subscriber gets the message, and on a plant network that can include devices that act on it. With retain=true the broker keeps the message and hands it to every future subscriber. For Sparkplug B topics (spBv1.0/...) use publish_sparkplug, which encodes the protobuf payload.

Sent at most once. success:true (meta.outcome 'written') means: QoS 0 written to the network, which the broker does not acknowledge; QoS 1/2 acknowledged by the broker (a broker acknowledges even a publish its ACL silently drops). Neither says that anyone acted on it. meta.outcome 'not_sent' means nothing left the server. 'unknown' (meta.code 'outcome_unknown') means it may have reached the broker: the server never sends it again, so check before retrying.

topic.description: Topic name to publish to, without wildcards ('+', '#'), e.g. 'sensors/temp'.

payload.description: Message text, sent as UTF-8. Binary payloads are not supported.

qos.description: 0: written to the network once, not acknowledged. 1: acknowledged by the broker (PUBACK). 2: acknowledged by the broker (PUBCOMP). Default 0. Whatever the QoS, this server sends the message at most once.

retain.description: Keep the message on the broker as the topic's retained message, which every future subscriber receives at once. Default false.

delivery.description: What the success confirms about delivery.

error.description: What went wrong, when success is false.

code.description: Why the call failed; set whenever success is false. See the contract's errors.

outcome.description: written: sent (QoS 1/2: acknowledged). not_sent: nothing left the server. unknown: it may have reached the broker; check before retrying. rejected: an explicit refusal that guarantees nothing was applied (never reported over MQTT 3.1.1).

request_sent.description: Whether the request may have left the server; null means an unexpected failure prevented dispatch tracking. Treat a null value as an unknown outcome and check before retrying.

errors.$comment: Every meta.code a failed call (success:false) can carry, and what to do about it. A client should branch on meta.code, never on the wording of error. Each tool's outputSchema lists these codes, and a failed result always has one.
errors.invalid_arguments: An argument is missing, has the wrong type or is out of range; error names it. Nothing was sent. Fix the arguments and call again.
errors.writes_disabled: This server is read-only: MQTT_WRITES_ENABLED is not true. Nothing was sent. Only whoever runs the server can enable writes, so do not retry.
errors.policy_denied: The deployment policy (MQTT_POLICY_FILE) does not allow this tool or operation. Nothing was sent.
errors.resource_limit: Too many calls are in flight, or the request is too large. Nothing was sent. Retry once running calls finish, or send less.
errors.audit_unavailable: The audit log (audit_path) could not record the write's intent, so the write was refused. Nothing was sent.
errors.endpoint_offline: The broker could not be reached, or the connection dropped before anything was written. Nothing was sent; the server keeps reconnecting in the background. Check get_broker_info and call again once connected is true.
errors.deadline_exceeded: The call ran out of time (MQTT_TOOL_TIMEOUT) before anything was sent. Nothing was sent, and it will not be sent later.
errors.cancelled: The MCP client cancelled the call or disconnected, or the server is shutting down. Nothing was sent.
errors.outcome_unknown: The message may have reached the broker (meta.outcome 'unknown'). The server never sends it again. Check its effect first, for example a device's next DDATA through read_messages, before calling again.
errors.send_failed: The MQTT client could not send the request. Nothing was sent.
errors.broker_refused: The broker refused the request, for example a subscription its ACL forbids.
errors.not_born: This server's Sparkplug B edge node, or the device, is not born: publish NBIRTH (and DBIRTH for a device) with publish_sparkplug first. Nothing was sent.
errors.not_subscribed: This server holds no subscription with exactly that filter; list_subscriptions shows the ones it holds.
errors.internal_error: An unexpected error inside this server. It is logged on the server's stderr.
